items.title: Can Agentic Robotics Solve Robotics’ Data-Scaling Problem?
items.summary: AI agents can utilize simulation to solve complex robotics problems using code instead of relying solely on large datasets. An example shows an agentic robotic arm successfully depositing used hypodermic needles into a disposal box by navigating variable subchallenges, like different box shapes. This approach suggests a potential method for addressing the data-scaling problem in robotics. Agentic systems leverage simulation to enable agents to learn and execute complex physical tasks. Therefore, agentic robotics offers a new paradigm for tackling data limitations in the field.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Can Agentic Robotics Solve Robotics’ Data-Scaling Problem?". This story explores how artificial intelligence agents can utilize simulation to solve complex robotics problems by relying on code rather than solely on large datasets. An example demonstrated an agentic robotic arm successfully depositing used hypodermic needles into a disposal box by navigating variable subchallenges, such as different box shapes. Agentic systems leverage simulation to enable agents to learn and execute complex physical tasks, suggesting a potential method for addressing the data-scaling problem in robotics through this new paradigm. This approach indicates a pathway for overcoming data limitations in the field of robotics. The development points toward increased capability for autonomous physical task execution in complex environments.

items.title: NVIDIA launches GR00T 2 and Isaac Lab 3.0 at CoRL
items.summary: NVIDIA introduced GR00T 2, an updated open frontier world action model, and Isaac Lab 3.0, the latest open-source robot learning framework, at CoRL. GR00T 2 enables robots to learn dexterous manipulation skills from diverse data and transfer skills between bodies. Isaac Lab 3.0, integrated with Newton, allows for efficient, parallel simulation training using accurate physics for complex robotic systems. New benchmarks like DexBench and VABAR are emerging to measure robot dexterity across industrial tasks. Various partners are already leveraging these technologies to advance robotics research and industrial applications.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, NVIDIA launches GR00T 2 and Isaac Lab 3.0 at CoRL. This report details the introduction of the updated open frontier world action model GR00T 2 and the latest open-source robot learning framework Isaac Lab 3.0 at the CoRL conference. GR00T 2 facilitates the learning of dexterous manipulation skills from diverse data and enables skill transfer between different robotic bodies. Isaac Lab 3.0, integrated with Newton, supports efficient and parallel simulation training for complex robotic systems using accurate physics. New evaluation benchmarks such as DexBench and VABAR are currently emerging to quantify robot dexterity across industrial applications. These advancements are being utilized by various partners in robotics research and industrial deployment. The developments signal progression in enabling more capable and adaptable robotic systems for practical tasks.

items.title: Nature Will launches 50-billion-parameter AI model for dexterous robot hands
items.summary: Nature Will launched Natura-1, a 50-billion-parameter physical general foundation model for dexterous hand control. This model was pre-trained on over a million hours of egocentric human data to combine instruction following with the ability to manipulate under changing conditions. Natura-1 learns to connect human intent to physical action through multimodal training on language, images, video, and actions. It operates with a 100-millisecond control loop to unify language, vision, and high-degree-of-freedom action. This work represents a step toward general foundation models capable of interacting effectively with the real world through physical manipulation.

This achievement was accomplished through multimodal training involving language, images, video, and physical actions. items.title: Practice Makes Precise: At CoRL, NVIDIA and Partners Reveal How Robots Rehearse Delicate Work in Simulation
items.summary: NVIDIA and partners at CoRL demonstrated methods for training robots to perform delicate manipulation tasks through simulation. World action models like GR00T 2 enable robots to learn dexterous skills by leveraging diverse data and skill transfer. The Isaac Lab framework, integrating accurate physics, allows for scalable training in simulation using agents and tools like Newton. Agentic robotics, such as the Graph-as-Policy framework, helps coordinate multiple skills into complex robot programs. These advancements, supported by benchmarks like DexBench, aim to bridge the gap between simulation and real-world industrial deployment.

The demonstration utilized world action models such as GR00T 2 to enable robots to learn dexterous skills by utilizing diverse data and skill transfer. The Isaac Lab framework was employed, integrating accurate physics to facilitate scalable training within simulation environments using agents and tools like Newton. items.title: Atlas On a Roll
items.summary: A Controls Engineer used the Atlas robot to test the limits of its actuators by retrofitting wheels onto the robot's feet. This experiment aimed to see how a learned whole-body controller could work with real, load-bearing hardware, pushing the motors to their performance envelopes. The process involved creating motion trajectories from human data and training a reinforcement learning policy to control the rolling motion. The work highlighted the necessity of closing the simulation-to-real gap by ensuring simulated motor behavior accurately reflected the physical hardware. Ultimately, this project demonstrated the synergistic relationship between low-level motor control and high-level reinforcement learning.

items.title: Boston Dynamics adds wheels to Atlas humanoid to test whole-body control
items.summary: Boston Dynamics attached wheels to its Atlas humanoid to test whole-body control, merging physics-based motor control with reinforcement learning. This experiment aimed to improve dynamic stability across unstructured terrain by allowing Atlas to process real-time feedback. Atlas demonstrated the ability to switch smoothly between rolling on flat surfaces and articulated legged motion over obstacles. The process involved a simple retrofit of an off-the-shelf scooter rim onto the ankle actuator. The research emphasizes that combining classical control with whole-body RL yields superior real-world agility.

items.title: ANYbotics begins deliveries of ANYmal X robot for hazardous industrial environments
items.summary: ANYbotics has started delivering its ANYmal X quadruped robot for use in hazardous industrial environments like oil, gas, and chemical facilities. This legged inspection system autonomously examines assets by using thermal cameras, acoustic sensors, and gas detectors to find potential issues. The robot is engineered to meet ATEX and IECEx explosion-protection standards through features like nitrogen-filled enclosures and flameproof protection for its components. ANYmal X operates with Shift software to integrate inspection data directly with industrial maintenance systems such as SAP. Early customers include Equinor and DSM-Firmenich, and major energy companies like BP and Shell have participated in testing.

items.title: Opinion: Supervised autonomy in robotics starts with the robot’s worst day
items.summary: Supervised autonomy requires designing for the robot's worst day, focusing on handling unforeseen situations rather than just smooth operation. Exceptions must be inventoried, with some resolved autonomously and others always requiring human intervention, especially for safety or customer rules. Requests for help must include context, confidence estimates, and time constraints to effectively involve supervisors. A clear supervisor role is necessary, balancing robot autonomy with human oversight through data-driven ratios and new skills. Documenting these limits protects operators commercially and addresses concerns regarding trust in autonomous systems.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Opinion: Supervised autonomy in robotics starts with the robot’s worst day". This segment discusses the necessity of designing supervised autonomy by focusing on handling unforeseen situations rather than just smooth operation. The methodology involves inventorizing exceptions where autonomy fails, with some exceptions resolved autonomously and others mandating human intervention, particularly concerning safety or customer rules. Requests for assistance require providing context, confidence estimates, and time constraints to effectively engage supervisors. A clear supervisor role must be established to balance robot autonomy with human oversight through data-driven ratios and the development of new skills. Documenting these operational limits serves to protect commercial interests and addresses trust concerns in autonomous systems. This work indicates a shift toward robust safety protocols in autonomous systems.

items.title: Make a Robot Arm Feel Weightless with NVIDIA Holoscan 5
items.summary: NVIDIA Holoscan 5 enables low-latency robotic control and high-throughput perception through a unified programming model for CPU and GPU workloads. A gravity-compensation loop was demonstrated using three custom Holoscan operators to calculate inverse dynamics with Pinocchio and command a reBot arm. The framework uses execution partitions and drop-oldest queues to minimize latency and jitter in the control path. Profiling with Nsight Systems showed that pinning the control partition significantly reduced p99.99 latency for both C++ and Python implementations. This approach forms a foundation for building more complex systems like hand-guided teaching and manipulation.

items.title: Welcome, UM1 Evo!
items.summary: UM1 Evo is a biomechanical robotic hand developed by Didier Vançon. It scored 6 out of 10 overall, highlighting its dexterity over raw strength, with a perfect 5/5 rating for Degrees of Freedom and a 1/5 for Strength. The hand weighs 1.7 kilograms and features 25 electric actuators assembled from custom CNC machined parts. Vançon spent five and a half years developing the prototype by integrating biomechanics, manufacturing, electronics, and software. The project aims to commercialize the prototype and knowledge for applications like prosthetics and humanoid robotics.

items.title: The Human Layer of the Automated Factory: Keeping People Informed on the Floor
items.summary: Workers must be kept informed about changes in automated factory layouts, robot cell locations, and autonomous mobile robot routes to ensure safe and efficient operations. Automation causes more frequent changes than traditional lines, necessitating a faster method of communication than paper notices. Digital signage offers a flexible way to display dynamic, high-contrast information like production targets and safety messages at the point of work. These displays should be integrated with live automation data, such as output counts, to provide accurate, relevant updates. Ultimately, screens help the human element of the factory keep pace with the rapid evolution of machinery.

items.title: Robotic Car Charger Locks On With Suction
items.summary: A robotic car charger uses suction cups to firmly attach to the vehicle while charging. The robot utilizes API calls to remotely unlock and open the charging port, bypassing potential wireless attacks. It uses Mecanum wheels and LiDAR for positioning, and an onboard camera with ChARuco patterns for fine-tuning alignment. Suction cups and a gear assembly are used to apply the necessary force to plug in the charger. The robot can also retract by swiveling its camera to see wall markers for parking.

Participants were encouraged to propose solutions for tasks involving repetitive lifting, hazardous environments, and ergonomic risks. items.title: Welcome, Anigon!
items.summary: Anigon is an industrial wheeled humanoid developed by Aimbo Robotics for logistics, manufacturing, and warehouse environments. It stands 189 cm tall, features force-controlled arms with 28 degrees of freedom, and includes tactile sensing and RGB depth cameras for object interaction. Supported capabilities include obstacle avoidance, sorting goods, and product assembly, utilizing its mobile base and manipulation hardware. The robot is equipped with hot-swappable batteries and safety features like collision detection and electromagnetic brakes. Anigon is currently a prototype with enterprise software integration capabilities, though its skill scores indicate development in navigation and manipulation.

items.title: Welcome, X Hand M1!
items.summary: X Hand M1 is a rigid robotic hand manufactured by Yuequan Bionics in Beijing, China, designed for industrial applications following human hand proportions. It features five fingers, measures 190 x 90 x 35 mm, and weighs 0.6 kg. The hand received a Humanoid.Guide Hand Score of 5 out of 10, indicating it is a developing option rather than a top-rated product. Component ratings suggest moderate degrees of freedom and lower strength, emphasizing the need for task-specific evaluation. The product is listed as in production with an advertised price of USD 7,000.

This development signals ongoing progress in the creation of functional, anthropomorphic robotic components for advanced industrial deployment.

items.title: Welcome, FF Nova!
items.summary: FF Nova is a compact humanoid robot from Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc., priced at $2,490, designed for developers, educators, and researchers. It features 20 degrees of freedom, electric servo actuators, and sensing capabilities including a camera, ToF sensor, and 2D LiDAR. Demonstrated skills include obstacle avoidance and standing up after a fall, positioning it as an introductory educational platform. The robot has limited navigation and manipulation skills, indicating it is a starting point for exploration rather than a mature system. It supports development via an open SDK and provides hardware for studying environmental perception and balance recovery.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, FF Nova!". The system supports development through an open software development kit and provides hardware for studying environmental perception and balance recovery. This development indicates a focus on foundational skills in robotic systems for further exploration.

items.title: Welcome, Star!
items.summary: Star is a 172 cm tall, 72 kg bipedal humanoid robot developed by TOPSTAR Group for industrial manufacturing. It features seven-axis arms with a dual arm payload capacity of 10 kg and 32 degrees of freedom. The robot can walk at a speed of 3 km/h and has demonstrated capabilities in obstacle avoidance and sorting goods. Currently, its skill score is low, with navigation and manipulation rated at preliminary levels. Star is positioned as an early-stage prototype exploring a humanoid format for factory automation.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Star!". This report details the specifications and current status of Star, a humanoid robot developed for industrial manufacturing. The robot is capable of walking at a speed of three kilometers per hour and has demonstrated abilities in obstacle avoidance and sorting goods. Current assessments indicate that the robot's skill score is low, with navigation and manipulation capabilities rated at preliminary levels, positioning Star as an early-stage prototype investigating a humanoid format for factory automation. This development indicates ongoing exploration into the practical application of humanoid robotics within automated manufacturing environments.

items.title: Welcome, KAIST!
items.summary: KAIST is a 165 cm tall, 75 kg humanoid research prototype developed by the Dynamic Robot Control and Design Lab. It demonstrates capabilities in obstacle avoidance, running 100 m, walking stairs, and jumping and landing. The robot's Humanoid Guide Skill Score is 4/10, with navigation rated 4/5 and manipulation rated 0/5, highlighting its strength in mobility. It utilizes internally developed components and reinforcement learning for its control system. The prototype is intended primarily for research, with a listed price of USD 150,000.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, KAIST!". The prototype measures one hundred sixty-five centimeters tall and weighs seventy-five kilograms and exhibits abilities in obstacle avoidance, running one hundred meters, ascending stairs, and performing jumps and landings. The robot's Humanoid Guide Skill Score is recorded at four out of ten, with navigation rated four out of five and manipulation rated zero out of five, indicating a primary strength in mobility. The system utilizes internally developed components and reinforcement learning for its control mechanisms, with the prototype having a listed price of one hundred fifty thousand US dollars and being designated for research purposes. This advancement signals ongoing progress in the integration of complex physical movement into advanced robotics research.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: TC-PEBRAS is hosting a video competition! $250 awards, 3 min videos, due Dec 12, 2026
items.summary: TC-PEBRAS is hosting a video competition to educate a general audience about robot performance evaluation and benchmarking. Participants must create 3-minute videos covering topics like metrics, test methods, and reproducibility in robotics and automation. Submissions are due by December 12, 2026, via email to tc.pebras.video@gmail.com. Four $250 awards will be given for general scope and Humanoids 2026 activities. The competition opens on November 5, 2026, with winners announced on December 17, 2026.

items.title: Machinery Positioning Options For Fabrication Facilities: A 2026 Shortlist For Industrial Buyers
items.summary: The best machinery positioning method depends on meeting four documented requirements: clearance, load, movement, and floor condition. Options include hydraulic toe jacks, low-profile machinery sliders, wheeled skates, air casters, overhead cranes, and forklifts. Buyers should evaluate positioning equipment against these four criteria for each move rather than defaulting to available tools. Machinery sliders offer a low-profile solution for tight spaces and can be used with multidirectional styles for maneuvering. A comprehensive move checklist should include weight, clearance, floor capacity, debris removal, and alignment plans.

items.title: Axon Invests $1.2B in Skydio, Gets Exclusive Drone Rights
items.summary: Axon invested $1.2 billion in drone maker Skydio and secured exclusive public safety distribution rights in the U.S. and Canada. This investment increased Axon's stake in Skydio to 37%. The deal, agreed upon on November 5, 2026, valued Skydio at $5.2 billion prior to the investment. Axon's payment consisted of 60% cash and 40% stock, funded partly by $1.15 billion in convertible notes. Skydio will remain independent, focusing on autonomous flight while Axon gains a significant sales channel.

items.title: How to minimize Wi-Fi roaming interruptions for autonomous mobile robots
items.summary: Autonomous mobile robots require reliable, fast Wi-Fi roaming to maintain real-time connectivity while moving between coverage zones. Traditional Wi-Fi causes interruptions because the main radio must stop traffic to search for new access points, leading to latency and packet loss. A dedicated scanning architecture, like Synaptics Scan Core, separates network discovery from application traffic using a low-power subsystem. This separation allows for faster roaming decisions, lower latency, and improved power efficiency. Implementing dedicated scanning enhances mobile robot performance by enabling continuous network awareness and faster transitions.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, "How to minimize Wi-Fi roaming interruptions for autonomous mobile robots". This report details methods for autonomous mobile robots to achieve reliable and fast Wi-Fi roaming by mitigating interruptions caused by traditional network searching. A dedicated scanning architecture, exemplified by the Synaptics Scan Core, separates network discovery from application traffic through a low-power subsystem. This separation enables faster roaming decisions and reduces latency and packet loss during transitions between coverage zones. Implementing this dedicated scanning mechanism allows for continuous network awareness, thereby enhancing the overall performance of mobile robots. This advancement signifies a path toward more robust and efficient wireless communication for autonomous systems.

items.title: Robbyant Open-Sources LingBot-Touch, One Tactile Model for Three Sensor Types
items.summary: Robbyant open-sourced LingBot-Touch, a tactile model that unifies signals from magnetic, visuotactile, and piezoresistive sensors into shared tactile tokens. This model was pretrained on nearly five thousand hours of touch recordings from human operators. Integrating these tokens into robot policies significantly increased success rates across various real-robot tasks compared to using raw sensor data. The research demonstrated that the tactile tokens provided substantial gains for models like LingBot-VLA and T-Rex. Limitations include testing only two hands and a focus on fingertip contact, as well as the exclusion of capacitive sensors from the pretraining data.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, Robbyant Open-Sources LingBot-Touch, One Tactile Model for Three Sensor Types. The research involved training the model on nearly five thousand hours of touch recordings from human operators to create these tactile tokens, which were then integrated into policies for models such as LingBot-VLA and T-Rex, showing substantial performance gains. This work indicates a pathway for more robust tactile perception in robotic systems.

items.title: Welcome, Avatar!
items.summary: Avatar is a wheeled humanoid prototype from Honda R&D Co., Ltd. designed for remote physical work, featuring two arms with five-fingered hands. It measures 155 cm tall, weighs 101 kg, and has a limited skill score of 3/10, placing it in the developing range. The system utilizes tactile feedback and visual cameras to allow operators to remotely guide the robot in tasks like sorting and assembly. Operator interaction is facilitated via a VR headset and gloves, with AI assisting in executing fine motions. Honda intends to apply Avatar in areas such as medical support, equipment maintenance, and disaster response.
